laat_vaar.blok: Stysel in die kos wat ons eet
laat_vaar.na: as mense stysel daarby gevoeg het
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'dit' can be read as the sausage rather than the starch; naming the starch makes the reference clear without changing the meaning (differs from the rejected 'wat mense bygevoeg het' change).
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: In 'kan wel stysel bevat as mense dit bygevoeg het' the pronoun can only sensibly mean the starch (people do not add the sausage), so the original is clear, and the proposal repeats 'stysel' twice in one sentence and makes it longer without making it clearly better.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: uit sy kos, en ook 'n dier wat die plant eet
laat_vaar_vorige.na: uit sy kos, en 'n dier wat die plant eet, kry dit ook
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The tacked-on phrase without its own verb reads awkwardly; giving it a verb makes a proper second clause that justifies the comma.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The elliptical 'en ook 'n dier wat die plant eet' is acceptable Afrikaans, while the proposal is longer and its 'dit' could point to either 'energie' or 'kos'.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Stysel in die kos wat ons eet
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: kan wel stysel bevat as mense dit bygevoeg het
laat_vaar_vorige.na: kan wel stysel bevat wat mense bygevoeg het
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'dit' can be read as the sausage rather than the starch; a relative clause makes clear it is the starch that was added.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'dit' naturally points to the starch, and swapping conditional 'as' for relative 'wat' drops the condition that starch is there only if people added it.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: dié in die suikerpot by die huis
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The lesson addresses the learner as 'jy' throughout, so the sudden plural 'julle' is inconsistent; this keeps the household meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'julle suikerpot' is natural Afrikaans for the household's sugar pot even when one child is addressed, so this is a lateral move, and 'dié in die suikerpot' stacks two near-identical words.
